legend: After arriving at Mary's house, Ian gifted a ring of flowers to Mary. The ring of flowers consists of different kinds of flowers. For convenience, we assign a number to each kind of flower and denote the ring by an array of integers a1,a2,...,an$$$a_1,a_2,...,a_n$$$ where n$$$n$$$ is the number of flowers in the ring, such that ai=aj$$$a_i=a_j$$$ if and only if the i$$$i$$$-th flower is of the same kind as the j$$$j$$$-th flower.

Mary calls a ring of flowers supreme if, for any two adjacent flowers, their kinds are not the same. Note that the n$$$n$$$-th flower is adjacent to the first flower. In other words, there does not exist i$$$i$$$ such that ai=ai+1$$$a_i=a_{i+1}$$$ with indices taken modulo n$$$n$$$. An exception to this is that a ring which consists of only 1$$$1$$$ flower is always regarded as supreme.

Mary wants to cut the ring of flowers which Ian had gifted her into several chains of flowers, and form a new ring of flowers with each chain by joining both of its ends. She wants all of the newly formed rings to be supreme. What is the minimum number of rings Mary needs to form to meet her requirement?
input: The first line consists of an integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤104$$$1\le t\le 10^4$$$), the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case consists of a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤3⋅105$$$1\le n\le 3\cdot10^5$$$), the number of flowers in the ring.
The second line of each test case consists of n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,...,an$$$a_1,a_2,...,a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤n$$$1\le a_i\le n$$$), where ai$$$a_i$$$ is the kind of the i$$$i$$$-th flower.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed 3⋅105$$$3\cdot10^5$$$.
Tests in subtasks are numbered 1−20$$$1 - 20$$$ with samples skipped. Each test is worth 10020=5$$$\frac{100}{20} = 5$$$ points.
output: For each test case, output an integer, the minimum number of rings that Mary needs to form such that all rings are supreme.
note: Explanation for the first three cases: (Note that the number on the circle representing the i$$$i$$$-th flower is i$$$i$$$, and the background colour of the circle is green if ai=1$$$a_i=1$$$, and blue if ai=2$$$a_i=2$$$.)
Case 1: The ring is already supreme. So the answer is 1$$$1$$$.
Case 2: The optimal way is to have three rings, each with one flower in it. So the answer is 3$$$3$$$.
Case 3: We can cut between flower 1$$$1$$$ and 4$$$4$$$, and between flower 2$$$2$$$ and 3$$$3$$$, to attain the optimal number of two rings. The answer is 2$$$2$$$.

legend.ai: Ian 到达 Mary 家后，送给 Mary 一个花环。这个花环由不同种类的花组成。为方便起见，我们为每种花分配一个编号，并用整数数组 a1,a2,...,an$$$a_1,a_2,...,a_n$$$ 表示这个花环，其中 n$$$n$$$ 是花环中花的数量，并满足 ai=aj$$$a_i=a_j$$$ 当且仅当第 i$$$i$$$ 朵花与第 j$$$j$$$ 朵花属于同一种类。
如果任意两朵相邻的花种类都不相同，Mary 就称这个花环是完美的。注意，第 n$$$n$$$ 朵花与第一朵花相邻。换句话说，不存在 i$$$i$$$ 使得 ai=ai+1$$$a_i=a_{i+1}$$$，其中下标按模 n$$$n$$$ 计算。例外是，仅由 1$$$1$$$ 朵花组成的花环始终被视为完美的。
Mary 想把 Ian 送给她的花环剪成若干条花链，并将每条花链的两端连接起来，分别形成新的花环。她希望所有新形成的花环都是完美的。为满足她的要求，Mary 至少需要形成多少个花环？

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 t$$$t$$$(1≤t≤104$$$1\le t\le 10^4$$$)，表示测试用例的数量。
每个测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤3⋅105$$$1\le n\le 3\cdot10^5$$$)，表示花环中花的数量。
每个测试用例的第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 a1,a2,...,an$$$a_1,a_2,...,a_n$$$(1≤ai≤n$$$1\le a_i\le n$$$)，其中 ai$$$a_i$$$ 是第 i$$$i$$$ 朵花的种类。
保证所有测试用例中 n$$$n$$$ 的总和不超过 3⋅105$$$3\cdot10^5$$$。
除去样例，子任务中的测试编号为 1−20$$$1 - 20$$$。每个测试点的分值为 10020=5$$$\frac{100}{20} = 5$$$ 分。

output.ai: 对于每个测试用例，输出一个整数，表示 Mary 需要组成的环的最少数量，使得所有环都是至高无上的。

note.ai: 前三个样例的解释：(注意，表示第 i$$$i$$$ 朵花的圆圈上的数字是 i$$$i$$$；当 ai=1$$$a_i=1$$$ 时，圆圈的背景颜色为绿色，当 ai=2$$$a_i=2$$$ 时为蓝色。)
样例 1：该圆环已经处于最优状态。因此答案为 1$$$1$$$。
样例 2：最优做法是得到三个圆环，每个圆环中有一朵花。因此答案为 3$$$3$$$。
样例 3：我们可以在花朵 1$$$1$$$ 和 4$$$4$$$ 之间，以及花朵 2$$$2$$$ 和 3$$$3$$$ 之间切割，从而得到最优的两个圆环。答案为 2$$$2$$$。
